clue.text: Offer to support old girl?

parts.note: to prop something is to support it
Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to offer help to an elderly woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the surface's whimsy: the 'offer' sounds like helping, but it is a proposal of marriage or a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is something put forward for acceptance, a synonym of an offer.

clue.text: Island raised capital for colony once

parts.note: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Aegean

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, as does the exclamation 'capital!'; the digit 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: An island's money was put up to fund a former colony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money or a city; here it is the old exclamation of approval, A1, turned upwards to give IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodesia was the British colony in southern Africa now known as Zimbabwe (and earlier Zambia too).

clue.text: Extravagant stimulus to single girl

parts.note: a prod is a poke or nudge that stirs someone to act
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: An encouragement given to an unmarried young woman seems lavish.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigal means wastefully lavish, as in the parable's spendthrift son.

clue.text: Basking, absorbing temperature that's amazing

indicators.note: absorbing means taking something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: sunning oneself is basking in the sunshine

explanation.surface: Lying in the sun and soaking up the heat is wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Stunning is a colloquial synonym for astonishing or amazing.

clue.text: Presumably look solemn before judge is to dismiss suit peremptorily

definitions.meaning: facing the judge one keeps a straight face, so any laughing is done outside the courtroom
to throw out a legal case with contempt, without hearing it seriously

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is whimsical: read the phrase literally, as laughing only when outside the court.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to treat a claim as so absurd that it is dismissed out of hand.

clue.text: Animal has a search in cellar

parts.note: a cat is an animal
to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

explanation.surface: A pet hunts around in the basement.
explanation.definitionFit: A catacomb is an underground chamber, and in older usage specifically a wine cellar or vault.

clue.text: Very short interval in concert

parts.note: sounds like a brief break during a performance, but means a tiny step in musical pitch

explanation.walkthrough: The 'interval' suggests a pause for drinks; in music an interval is the distance between two notes, and this is the smallest in Western scales.
explanation.definitionFit: A semitone, half a tone, is the smallest musical interval in the Western scale.

clue.text: Is supportive, but fails to intervene

definitions.meaning: to stand by someone is to remain loyal and support them
to stand by is also to watch idly without acting

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both loyal support and passive onlooking, two opposite-seeming idioms.

clue.text: Seeming rejection of father and mother, say

indicators.note: a rejection turns something back, so the word for father is read backwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a mother is an example of a parent, signalled by 'say'

explanation.surface: Someone appears to have spurned both their dad and their mum.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means seeming, as in an apparent success that may not be real.

clue.text: No opera house originally in island capital

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so this piece is placed first

parts.note: taken as written
Lulu is an opera by Alban Berg

explanation.surface: A remark that the island's capital city has no opera house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' looks like a first-letter signal on 'house'; instead it says the house piece comes first. Lulu, Berg's unfinished opera, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Honolulu, on the island of Oahu, is the capital of Hawaii.

clue.text: Extremely greedy, given fixed amount in revolution

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance of something

explanation.surface: Someone very greedy is given a set portion during a political uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' suggests politics; here it means spinning round.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyration is a whirling or circular movement, a revolution about a point.

clue.text: Daisy's face is remarkable — paint her

indicators.note: remarkable suggests something striking or out of the ordinary, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Daisy has an extraordinary face, so an artist should paint her.
explanation.walkthrough: Daisy looks like a woman's name; it is the flower, whose 'face' is its ring of petals.
explanation.definitionFit: The perianth is the outer part of a flower, petals and sepals together, which forms the face of a daisy.

clue.text: Some days, groups of whales will follow round other sea creatures

indicators.note: the whale groups come after the round letter

parts.note: Oct, October, is a set of days of the year
O is round in shape
a pod is a group of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: On certain days, schools of whales trail round other marine animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Other' acknowledges that whales are sea creatures too.
explanation.definitionFit: Octopods are eight-armed cephalopods, octopuses and their kin, which live in the sea.

clue.text: Scandalous amount taken in old window tax?

definitions.meaning: an outrageous overcharge or swindle in plain view
Britain once taxed houses by their number of windows, so the levy literally took money for letting light in

explanation.walkthrough: The window tax (1696 to 1851) taxed British homes by the number of windows; the question mark flags the literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a blatant overcharge, robbery committed openly in broad light.

clue.text: Plain daughter's intuition man finally ignored

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter; the 's is a link

indicators.note: ignored means left out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: instinct is intuitive feeling

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word man

explanation.surface: A homely daughter's feminine intuition has been brushed aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an unflattering adjective for the daughter; it is the definition, meaning clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinct means clear or easily perceived, a synonym of plain.

clue.text: Yen, and yen again — making money

parts.note: Y is the symbol for the Japanese currency, the yen
earning is making money

explanation.surface: A trader keeps converting into Japanese currency, raking in profits.
explanation.walkthrough: The two yens do different jobs: the first is a longing, the definition; the second, flagged by 'again', is the currency, abbreviated Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A yen is a strong desire or longing, a synonym of yearning.

clue.text: Brave in run, outwardly cool

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: outwardly says the word for cool sits on the outside of the other piece

parts.note: tepid means lukewarm, slightly cool
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A runner who keeps an air of calm looks courageous.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means fearless, a synonym of brave.

clue.text: From start of race I step out, leaving the beaten track

parts.note: 'the off' is the start of a horse race

indicators.note: out suggests disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A skier pushes off from the start line and leaves the groomed run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' could be a container or deletion signal; it rearranges I STEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-piste skiing is done away from the prepared runs, and figuratively it means departing from the usual path.

clue.text: Support, it's said, a blackleg would find a bit of a gamble

indicators.note: it's said marks a word pronounced like another, here with the R silent

parts.note: a backer gives support, especially financial
a rat is a strike-breaker, a blackleg

explanation.surface: A strike-breaker would find staking money on him a bit of a risk.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech BACKER sounds like BACCA.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a casino card game played for stakes, a form of gambling.

clue.text: Arrest in struggle, and use handcuffs?

indicators.note: a struggle is a confused tussle, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Police make an arrest during a scuffle and cuff the suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows handcuffs are only one way to hold someone back.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back or confine, which handcuffing does to a person.

clue.text: Make first move as particularly brilliant aristocrat

parts.note: a star is an outstanding, brilliant performer
toff is British slang for an upper-class person

explanation.surface: A dazzling nobleman takes the initiative.
explanation.definitionFit: To start off is to begin, making the first move in something.

clue.text: Put a limit on a conurbation that's maximum size

parts.note: to cap something is to set an upper limit on it
a conurbation is a large urban area, a city

explanation.surface: Planners restrict the growth of a sprawling urban area.
explanation.definitionFit: Capacity is the most that something can hold, its maximum size.

clue.text: Suggestion hotel faces ruin, allowing drug in

indicators.note: faces means stands in front of, so the hotel word comes before the next piece

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel

indicators.note: in says the drug goes inside the word for ruin

parts.note: to undo is to ruin or bring down
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A hotel is threatened with ruin by letting drugs on the premises.
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is an indirect suggestion or insinuation.

clue.text: Puts out some papers opposing current tendencies

indicators.note: out suggests disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A newspaper group publishes articles against the fashion of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present-day'; here it is a flow of water, and going upstream is going against it.
explanation.definitionFit: Upstream means against the flow, used figuratively of going against prevailing trends.

clue.text: Councillor taken round in legal situation as judge

indicators.note: taken round means one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: in football a player is onside when in a legal position

explanation.surface: A local councillor sits as a judge in a legal matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The legal language suggests a court; it is the offside rule in football.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider is to weigh up or deem, as a judge does in assessing a matter.

clue.text: Making no charge for handling

definitions.meaning: paying for someone's food or drink so that they are not charged
dealing with or managing something, as in handling a subject

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers paying for another's entertainment and also dealing with a matter or patient.
